//: The case rows a seeded environment carries, one version of the
shared fixture. `seeds/dev.json` and `seeds/staging.json` name which
of these cases to load, into which firm, opened by which person;
this file says what each case contains.
SHAPE. Every body below is the JSON the API's own routes accept —
a debtor is the PUT /v1/cases/<id>/debtors/<role> body, a collection
item is the POST /v1/cases/<id>/<collection> body — and the loader
parses them with the same core/ functions those routes use, so a
malformed row fails with the API's own field errors and a rule that
tightens (provenance, say) breaks seeding loudly rather than writing
rows the service has stopped agreeing with.
NO IDS ARE PUBLISHED, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN. A case's id in an
environment is derived by the loader from the target table, the
firm and this file's `handle`, so two environments seed different
ids from the same fixture and a re-run finds the rows it wrote last
time instead of writing them again. An id written here would be an
id from someone else's environment.
EVERY VALUE IS SYNTHETIC. Nothing here describes a real person, a
real employer or a real account. `seed capture` refuses a source
that is not a dev stack for exactly this reason, and a review of a
diff to this file should ask the same question.
